memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the eighth day the boy is to be circumcised." - Lev 12:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short line, dropped into the middle of instructions for the mother. But it carries centuries behind it.

Circumcision was given to Abraham long before Moses (Gen 17:9-14). It was the sign of the covenant — the mark that this child belonged to the people God had claimed for Himself. Here in Leviticus, God simply reaffirms it. Even in the middle of a chapter about recovery and ritual, the covenant is not forgotten.

Notice the timing: the eighth day. The child had no say in it. He could not choose it, earn it, or understand it. The covenant sign was placed on him because of the family he had been born into, not because of anything he had done.

That is grace running through the whole story of Scripture. God chooses, God claims, God marks out — before we could ever contribute.

But the sign was always pointing beyond itself. Even Moses and the prophets called Israel to circumcise their hearts, not merely their bodies (Deut 30:6). And Paul says plainly that in Christ we have received a circumcision not performed by human hands — the putting off of the flesh, done by Christ Himself (Col 2:11).

The outward sign has given way to the inward reality. What God always wanted was not a mark on the body but a changed heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you relying on any outward religious mark rather than an inward change?
2. What does it mean to you that God claimed you before you could contribute anything?
3. Where is God calling for a heart change rather than an external adjustment?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You claimed me before I could offer You anything. Do the deeper work in me — not just outward religion, but a heart truly changed by Christ. Amen.
